frames.narration: The same order data is stored two ways. In SQL it is split into customers, orders and items tables. In the document store it is one self-contained document per order.
Task 1: show one order with its customer and items. SQL joins three tables.
The document store returns the whole order in a single read, because everything is stored together.
Task 2: a customer changes their address. In SQL the address lives in one place: one row is updated.
In the document store the address was copied into each of the customer's orders, so every one must be updated (and any missed copy is now wrong).

messages.label: update all of this customer's orders

frames.narration: Task 3: revenue per customer across everything. SQL was built for this: GROUP BY with an optimiser and indexes.
A document store can do it too, but with an aggregation pipeline or by reading every document and adding up in code.

Task 4: add a new field to new orders (a gift message). SQL needs a schema migration. The document store simply starts writing the field. There is no free lunch: each model makes some jobs cheap and others costly.
